title: a element defines content model as only Transparent
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-a-element
Defines Content model as:
> [Content model](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#concept-element-content-model):
[Transparent](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#transparent), but there must be no [interactive content](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#interactive-content-2) descendant, [a](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-a-element) element descendant, or descendant with the [tabindex](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#attr-tabindex) attribute specified.

The [Transparent content model](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#transparent) states:
> Some elements are described as transparent; they have "transparent" in the description of their content model.

This can be seen in some of the Transparent examples, for example: [ins](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/edits.html#the-ins-element) - Content model: Transparent

However a [span](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-span-element) is generally expected to be acceptable content of an anchor and it describes its categories as:
> _ Flow content.
> - Phrasing content.
> - Palpable content.


So either the `span` element is no longer a permitted decendent of an anchor, the `span` (and many others) are missing the Transparent modele in their category list, or the anchor is missing information about permitted content types.
